Exmos.(as) Senhor(as), 

Recebemos a vossa notificação para prestação de informações relativamente à Reclamação do(a) Sr.(a) Carmen Vieira (Motorista/Parceira)  – EDOC 1583/2023.

Tal como foi já respondido numa queixa anterior (EDOC 1255/2023), a ora Reclamante foi identificada como tendo um comportamento fraudulento na nossa plataforma, tendo repetidamente em inúmeras viagens que aceitou, confirmado na plataforma ter chegado ao local de recolha e dado início às viagem, após o que cancelava as mesmas sem motivo. 

De acordo com o artigo 8º da Lei n.o 45/2018 de 10 de agosto (Regime jurídico da atividade de transporte individual e remunerado de passageiros em veículos descaracterizados a partir de plataforma eletrónica),  “_Só podem ser recusados os serviços de TVDE que: a) Impliquem a circulação em vias manifestamente intransitáveis pelo difícil acesso ou em locais que ofereçam notório perigo para a segurança do veículo, dos passageiros ou do motorista; b) Sejam solicitados por pessoas com comportamento suspeito de perigosidade; c) Sejam solicitados de forma incompatível com o previsto na presente lei_.”

Em conformidade, os Termos e Condições (T&C)[ disponíveis na nosso website|https://bolt.eu/pt-pt/legal/new-terms-for-fleets/?category=rides] - que são aceites por todos os Operadores TVDE que utilizam a plataforma da Bolt - indicam que a Bolt reserva-se o direito de bloquear o acesso à plataforma, especificamente por razões de fraude ou não cumprimento da legislação em vigor relativa ao exercício da profissão de motorista de TVDE.

De acordo com as melhores práticas, enviámos atempadamente informação à ora Reclamante sobre o incumprimento verificado. Na última comunicação efetuada, foi ainda deixada a possibilidade de apresentar reclamação através do seu Operador TVDE,  sendo que o mesmo não o fez até ao dia de hoje.

Esperamos que a informação acima seja suficiente para esclarecer todas as questões mas mantemo-nos disponíveis para qualquer esclarecimento adicional.

Os melhores cumprimentos,

Hey, [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] !

There are mostly 2 cases:

* In some markets, we have a very high base fee, which makes earnings per km much more attractive if you are delivering short-distance orders;
* In some markets we increase minimum earnings during supply shocks, which again make short-distance orders much more desirable for couriers.

In these cases, car couriers tend to switch to bicycles. In some markets, couriers have noticed that if they choose motorbikes as delivery vehicles, they receive orders more frequently, this way maximising their earnings per hour. 

We have not disclosed our dispatching logic in detail, but couriers know that bicycle couriers should receive shorter distance orders, while cars long distances and from grocery shops. We have shared the main details only.

Thanks for the recommendations. We are specifically worried about Portugal and Malta - any specific recommendations for these markets? We plan to allow fleets to change vehicle type for couriers and we would still have the ability to do that from the OPS/CS side. Any concerns here?

Best regards,
Roberts

The table has 7 indexes, is this on purpose?
It seems like the indexing strategy was just to index to every column, which is not optimal way to index. While indexes can help reads tremendously, they hurt write performance, meaning there is a tradeoff. 
Please check this document to get an idea how indexes are used: [https://mysql.rjweb.org/doc.php/index_cookbook_mysql|https://mysql.rjweb.org/doc.php/index_cookbook_mysql|smart-link] 
If you know that SQL queries on this table will do look ups by one of the index columns only (WHERE indexed_column = value), then we can proceed. Otherwise, please considering adding only the indexes that are know to be used by SQL queries on this table.

* Section 4: “If the Contractual Partner does not collect removed bicycles *within a deadline set by the Municipality*, the Municipality may sell or give away the bicycles.” The Municipality is free to set any deadline and it could potentially be a very short one and if this deadline is not met it allows the Municipality to sell our Bolt bikes. 
* Section 6: “The technical measure with geofencing must be implemented by 01 March 2024 at the latest.” I understand that this is commercially approved? 
* Section 7: No personal data  or sensitive data is shared, is that correct? 
* Section 8: _“The Contractual Partner is responsible for covering the Municipality's expenses for transport, storage and administration in connection with the removal of the Contractual Partner's rental bicycles, cf. above on the placement of bicycles on public roads. Payment currently amounts to DKK 338 per bicycle._” The Municipality can increase the amounts whenever they want without notice. ´
* Section 9: Automatic extension is against our contract standards and should be prevented. We don’t know what our business will look like in a year and we don’t want to be locked into a contract by being passive. It is up to the local & business team to keep track of these automatic extensions and terminating the contract prior to the notice period, if necessary. 
* Section 11: “_The municipality has the right to require the agreement and its terms to be amended at any time with appropriate notice_.” Again, the agreement is very beneficial for the Municipality and allows them to essentially change the terms to whatever suits them. 
* Section 14: “_The Municipality cannot lose its ability to claim breach by inaction, even if the Municipality is aware that the Contractual Partner is in breach of the agreement and fails to invoke the breach_ *_until long after the matter came to the Municipality's knowledge_*.”  This allows the Municipality to make claims for a very long time and thereby increases Bolt’s dispute and claims risk. 
* Section 16: Liability for damages is unlimited under Danish law. This is directly in breach with Bolt’s contract standards and our liability should be limited to the contract value. However, the risk of liability claims under this specific agreement seems low. 
* Total number of bikes: agreement states 1300 but the Appendix states 1625, the correct number should be aligned in both parts. 

Essentially there are several terms that we should amend in the agreement to correspond to Bolt’s legal risk appetite, however, I understand it is a business critical agreement in order for Bolt to offer bikes in Copenhagen and if the business team is comfortable with the risks then we can proceed with signing. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

{code:sql}with base as (
select 
	a.id  as support_case_id
	,a.created as case_created_utc 
	,a.city_id 
	,a."source"
	,cast(a.order_id as bigint) as order_id
	,b.issue_key
from ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case as a
inner join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue_keys_updated as b
	on a.id = b.support_case_id 
	and b.issue_key in ('rider_lost_item','rider_lost_phone')
where 1=1
	and a.user_persona = 'rider'
	and date(a.created_date) >= date('2023-09-01')
	and date(a.created_date) < date('2023-12-01')
	and a.state not in ('duplicate','draft')
),
final_table as (
select 
	c.support_case_id
	,c.case_created_utc
	,c.issue_key
	,c.order_id
	,c.city_id
	,c.source
	,d.state as order_state
	,d.created as order_created_utc
	,e.created as order_finished_utc
	,date_diff('hour',e.created, c.case_created_utc) as hour_difference
	,f.created as order_finished_2_utc
	,date_diff('hour',f.created, c.case_created_utc) as hour_difference_2
from base as c
left join ng_public.company_order as d	
	on c.order_id = d.id 
	and c.city_id = d.city_id
	and date(d.created_date) >= date('2023-03-01')
left join ng_public.company_order_state_change_log  as e
	on c.order_id = e.order_id 
	and c.city_id = e.city_id 
	and e.to_state in ('finished','cancelled','no_driver_provided')
	and date(e.created_date) >= date('2023-03-01')
left join ng_public.company_order_event as f
	on c.order_id = f.order_id 
	and c.city_id = f.city_id 
	and f."type" in ('order_finished', 'order_cancelled','order_no_driver_provided')
	and date(f.created_date) >= date('2023-03-01') 
)
select
	support_case_id
	,case_created_utc
	,issue_key
	,order_id
	,city_id
	,"source"
	,order_state
	,order_created_utc
	,coalesce(order_finished_utc, order_finished_2_utc) as order_finished_utc
	,coalesce(hour_difference, hour_difference_2) as hour_difference_between_order_finish_and_case
	,case when coalesce(hour_difference, hour_difference_2) < 0 then 'not valid'
		when coalesce(hour_difference, hour_difference_2) > 0 and coalesce(hour_difference, hour_difference_2) < 24 then 'within 24 hours'
		when coalesce(hour_difference, hour_difference_2) >= 24 then 'after 24 hours'
		when coalesce(hour_difference, hour_difference_2) is null then 'no data' end as case_time_flag
from final_table{code}

# Assessment of driver medical docs: This is *NOT* a Legal question and we are not in a position to confirm this. The question relates to Driver docs and the the Driver is free to use such medical docs as a defence against a claim from the Rider but Bolt is not involved in this process (nor are we the Driver’s legal advisor). Also, Bolt should not assess any medical docs or similar from Drivers as this would pose a *direct reclassification risk* where we are imposing control and acting as “an employer”. Generally we should refrain from making any statements on the Driver’s liability vs. Rider’s liability unless it relates to something governed in our T&Cs and platform services.
# The driver’s legal liability depending on whether he is truly allergic or not: the answer to this question *does not relate to Bolt’s liability*. It is essentially a question for the Driver to assess on his end. Although we can communicate to the Rider that we don’t support discrimination and we are sorry they experienced what they did, any dispute or liability arising from it is to be sorted out between the Driver and Rider. Bolt does not get involved in the liability between the parties due to the provided transportation service as that service is provided without Bolt as a party and based on local laws (no written agreement).

On a separate note, apart from this ticket and *not* to be communicated to the driver, the liability for discrimination in this case and similar cases depends on a balancing excercize between (1) the disability causing the person to need a medical assistance dog vs (2) the type of allergy and how severe it is. This would be assessed on a case by case basis. As a platform company FI law may require that we facilitate non-discrimination, e.g. by making communication between Drivers and Riders regarding service animals possible some how. It might be good for Bolt to look into how we can make sure that Riders with medical assistance animals and Drivers both know what to do, while at the same time preventing that Riders who have Pets stop booking Pet category and ‘fake’ that they are assistance animals to pay less). However this is essentially a question to be initially looked at by Local Ops (with our support of course). 

I hope this answers your questions. Please let me know if you have any follow-ups or if we can close this ticket.

Ida

* Article 6a of the PID does not apply either to *real personalised price reductions* that do not have the nature of ‘announcing’ the price reduction. A typical example of such price reductions are those resulting from the consumer’s prior purchases with the seller concerned, such as when the consumer receives a ‘20 % off’ voucher upon the purchase, valid for the next purchase until end of the month. Other examples of real personalised price reductions falling outside the scope of Article 6a are reductions granted on special occasions for that consumer, such as upon signing up to the loyalty programme or on the consumer’s marriage or birthday, as well as reductions applied at the time of the purchase that have not been ‘announced’ in advance.
* In contrast, Article 6a of the [PID|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN-ET/TXT/?from=EN&uri=CELEX%3A01998L0006-20220528] will be applicable to those price reductions, which, even though presented as person­ alised, are in *reality offered/announced to consumers in general*. Such situation could occur where the trader makes available ‘vouchers’ or discount codes to potentially all consumers visiting the brick and mortar shop or the online shop during specific periods. Examples could be campaigns such as:
— ‘Today 20 % off when using the code XYZ’; or
— ‘This weekend 20 % off on everything for loyalty members only’.

where the code/the loyalty programme is accessible/used by many or the majority of customers. In these cases, the trader must comply with the requirements of Article 6a, i.e. ensuring that the ‘prior’ price for all the goods concerned is *their lowest publicly available price* in the last 30 days

{noformat}General rule: I didn't enable HPA on services with 100mCPU.

a) dispatch-pref
Downscaled. Enabled HPA where it makes sense.

b) dispatch-priority
Already 100mCPU.

c) ride-matching-*
Downscaled to 3 instances on every shard.
Enabled HPA where it makes sense.

> Increase number of partitions for more even load?

Max already did that.


> Opt-out from consolidation and HPA for less disruptions due to rebalancing?

I think having consolidation and rebalancing happening more often is OK.
Rebalancing is being completed pretty fast, so I think it is fine.


> Does HPA even makes sense if it's coupled to Kafka?

Yes, I think so. Why? Because Kafka rebalancing is fast.

Example: let's take rebalancing in some matching-worker process:
https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/r/s/Q5C3V
Time between rebalancing ("Kafka API error") and when the very next cluster being matched ("Cluster matching started") is about 1 sec.

In my opinion, HPA with current configuration may not work as expected in two scenarios:

scenario 1) when service has 100mCPU, so the volatility of "relative CPU usage" metric is high.
scenario 2) when service takes some time to spin up and consumes CPU during that period (like searchworker), and CPU spikes
during startup can be interpreted by HPA as indicator to spin up even more instances.


d) search-area
Increasing partitions count is in progress.
Enabled HPA where mCPU >= 250.

e) search-driver-details
Downscaled, enabled HPA.

f) went through "cluster info" and fixed warnings.
g) for non-HPA services: made sure that we have same instances count on two clusters

h) reviewed suggested T-shirt size. 
Applied where needed.
It changes often though, but at the moment of writing this I've fixed pretty much everything what's needed.


What's left:
a) Increase driver-polling partitions for Kafka
b) potentially, adjust container size and/or enable HPA in searcharea{noformat}

Hi Ahto and Mihai, 

Thank you both for reaching out!

I suppose this relates to services received by third party suppliers that are consumed at the level of local entities - which are then using/getting some sort of benefit from these services locally but invoices have been/are issued to Bolt Operations instead of Bolt local entities following the existing contracts.

For context, as you may already know, from a Tax and Transfer Pricing perspective, if some PR services provided by third parties benefit only the local market, those services should be invoiced to the local entity in question. On the other hand, if the services are provided for a regional/global benefit to multiple locations (e.g. to all CEE entities because those are part of a broader campaign/project that’s centrally managed from EE), that invoice can still be addressed to Bolt Operations.

The rationale behind is that we should recognise expenses in the legal entities that benefit from the services rendered by third parties. Furthermore, our tax structure is set up in such a way that local entities should bear the costs and recharge them back to Bolt Operations. In the end, Bolt Operations bears the costs but those should be allocated first to the local entity to generate revenue locally (via a mark-up that’s applied on the costs). Otherwise, tax authorities can argue that we’re avoiding taxes locally.

Now, to your specific question: 

I (as a tax person) do not mind much about the agreement but the invoices and which entity assumes the costs - because of the tax implications that may arise otherwise as explained above. Typically, supplier invoices follow the contract but maybe there's a way to get invoices in the correspondent local entity if needed, and keep the agreement as-is with Bolt Ops? It could be that signing a separate SOW, defining Bolt as the group in the contract, or something like that suffices? 

That’s what we’re doing at the moment with some tax suppliers and it works quite ok.

Please let me know if you have any follow-up questions. Happy to discuss on the call if you need as well.

Hello Krzysztof Mewes 

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

Bolt is not granting employees shares, but stock options or cash based units (CBUs). In Mexico employees are granted CBUs which means that when exercising is taking place then option holders will not receive shares of the company but the gain is in cash.

According to Bolt's Phantom Share Option Agreement units can be exercised 10 years after grant date and before that if the company so decides. Once 10 years has passed from the grant date then the option holder has 5 years to exercise their option units. To do that they need to Bolt. 
Bolt has the opportunity to offer early exercise possibility and in that case all eligible option holders will be reached out to notify them about such opportunity and set criteria.

Strike price is set when grant is made and it’s visible to option holders in Carta for each grant separately.

# The use case for using proxy is → Need to connect to public internet resources, with preserved IPs

Hi,

I have went through the Tax Authorities guidelines and the findings are the following:

VAT rate change from 20% to 22% affect all our invoices where we currently need to add EE 20%. Like RH invoices from the driver to the rider, domestic EE commission fee invoices, EE sales from Bolt Market etc. I believe that we don’t need to state invoice by invoice what we have there in the folder that this invoice will be affected and this invoice will not be affected? I mean if we just change in our systems the EE VAT rate then shouldn’t this information flow to all the affected invoices? 

When it comes to transitional rules then the following rules apply (sorry there was some misleading information above):

* If we issue an invoice in the new year for the services that were provided in 2023 and the invoice does not cover any period of 2023 then we have to apply the 20% VAT rate on the invoice.
* If we issue an invoice in the new year for the services that were provided in 2023 and also in 2024 then we have to apply the new rate (the example where the ride started 23.59 in the last day of the year and ended in new year).

The same goes for all affected invoices (also Drive, Delivery, rentals, B4B). So could we create a general rule that in any situation where:

* an invoice is issued for services that started and ended in 2023 20% VAT is applied.
* an invoice is issued for services that start in 2023 and carry on to 2024 or the services start in 2024 then 22% VAT is applied.
* if goods are sold (in Bolt Market) in 2023 then 20% is applied, if the goods are sold after midnight then 22% is applied.
* As for the restaurants' invoices - correct me if I’m wrong but I don’t think we generate actual invoices on their behalf in EE. If we do then the same logic applies as for market - if the invoice is issued for the food that is sold in 2023 then 20% applies.

Would that make sense?

Here are lots of examples about various situations here for background reading: [https://www.emta.ee/en/business-client/taxes-and-payment/value-added-tax#examples-01012024|https://www.emta.ee/en/business-client/taxes-and-payment/value-added-tax#examples-01012024|smart-link].

If there are any concrete invoicing flows that cause any questions then let us know we’ll be happy to help. Just seemed to us that looking and commenting all these invoices in the folder would not be the most efficient solution. Happy to discuss if you disagree.

Tanel

Is there anything specific that you are looking to include? 

We have one set of T&Cs for Sweden so the same applies to all rentals business in Sweden regardless of city. Further, we already have the following wording in the T&Cs: 

*_6.3 We reserve the right to offer liability insurance arrangement (“Insurance Cover”) in some or all Service Areas, to insure, subject to limitations and exceptions of the Insurance Cover, liability You incur in respect of injury to a third party or accidental damage to the physical property of a third party arising from Your use of the E-Vehicle._* _If, for any reason, You are not eligible for the Insurance Cover, then You understand and acknowledge that You assume liability for any and all costs caused by You to a third party, including without limitation costs of ambulance transport services, hospital stays and medical treatment._

This provides Bolt with the right to offer liability insurance but not with the obligation to do so and this can be restricted to some Service Areas (restriction to only Stockholm is already possible under the T&Cs). From a legal perspective we have deemed the current wording to be sufficient to allow us to provide insurance coverage wherever we see fit. 

From a practical point of view, you need to upload a insurance coverage certificate to our Legal landing page for Sweden (which can be found [here|https://bolt.eu/sv-se/legal/?category=micromobility]). Please see as an example the insurance certificates that are currently provided for Norway: [Motor Liability Certificate|https://bolt.eu/en-no/legal/terms-for-insurance-scooters/?category=micromobility], [General TP Liability|https://bolt.eu/en-no/legal/terms-for-insurance-ebikes/?category=micromobility]. 

Please cooperate with the insurance team [~accountid:62a3287576c0360069f59b72] to organise the correct certificates and uploading them on the website. Further, the information in the Passenger App needs to be updated with the correct information on insurance.

So as not to miss any information, below is short summary on conditions. 



*_Why is it possible for a taxi from Sweden to enter Denmark without meeting the legal requirements?_*



Sweden has special [+arrangements+|https://www.regeringen.se/contentassets/f70d91e2d57646c694b8216a94f43d0f/overenskommelse-jamte-tillaggsprotokoll-med-danmark-om-internationell-taxitrafik-pa-vag/] with Denmark, Norway and Finland. According to this arrangement a number of prerequisites have to be fulfilled which make it possible to transport passengers via taxi from one territory to the other. Article 3 states that

*  “_a taxi domiciled within the territory of one of the contracting parties which, in accordance with its national legislation, has the right to carry out taxi traffic between the territories of the contracting parties may carry out such traffic:_

(Furthermore according to paragraph 3 b)

* _A taxi company domiciled in Sweden may in Denmark pick up passengers at specially arranged taxi stations at the locations specified in the_ *_supplementary protocol._*



This article is the basis for exemption which makes certain trips from Sweden to Denmark, and vice versa, possible. More specifically the [+supplementary+|https://www.regeringen.se/contentassets/f70d91e2d57646c694b8216a94f43d0f/overenskommelse-jamte-tillaggsprotokoll-med-danmark-om-internationell-taxitrafik-pa-vag/] protocol, article 2a specifies that:



* _In accordance with Article 3, the Contracting Parties have agreed_

_that:_

_a) a taxi company domiciled in Sweden may in Denmark pick up passengers at_ *_specially organized taxi stands at Copenhagen Airport (Kastrup),_*



Furthermore regarding tax-issues, Sweden and Denmark have special [+arrangements+|https://tidningenkonsulten.se/foretagsaktuellt/taxi-fran-sverige-till-danmark-hur-blir-det-med-moms/#:~:text=I%20Sveriges%20respektive%20Danmarks%20anslutningsf%C3%B6rdrag,del%20B%2010%20i%20momsdirektivet).] to ease cross border business.

“_In Sweden's and Denmark's accession treaties to the EU, both countries in their various treaties have granted permission to instead apply tax exemption for the passenger transport in question (articles 371 and 380 respectively in combination with Annex X part B 10 of the VAT directive).”_

Furthermore “_Against this background, the Swedish taxi driver must not charge either Swedish or Danish VAT for the driving. The same applies if a drive takes place from Denmark to Sweden.”_

My apologies for the late response.

I’m working on it right now.

TL;DR Refunding Discount is hard, because the intention of the received request isn’t always clear.

Long answer: I think this described algorithm might not be good enough.

The reason for this is the following:

If the Order that was discounted (i.e. Partner price 15$, User pays 10$, Bolt covers 5$) receives a Refund Request 15$ Partner at Fault, we don’t know which of these situations is correct:

* It’s a Partner Full Refund, where he intends to return everything back (15$), so we can give user 10$ and *use 5$ to reverse the Bolt Discount*.
* It’s a well motivated reimbursment to the user of the amount 15$ (e.g. with Force Refund), and the User is supposed to receive 15$, *we can’t reverse the Bolt Discount*.

We could… maybe… use Refund Type (FULL/PARTIAL) but there’s trouble with multi-suborder orders. The order will be full-refunded suborder-by-suborder, so we would need to check the Refund Type of other Refunds…and what if they are mixed? …

Thank you for your patience - there was indeed a gap here. 

It is not possible to issue a refund without cancelling the subscription first. 

Once you cancel the subscription, the refund has to be done manually. 

If the rider wants to cancel the *trial* subscription, you can do so by cancelling the subscription (by choosing the _Cancel_ option, not _Instant Cancel_) and then issuing a refund.

If the rider wants to cancel the (non-trial) subscription within *14 days of purchase*, you can do so by cancelling the subscription (by choosing the _Cancel_ option, not _Instant Cancel_) and then issuing a refund; the rider should be informed that if they request a refund after subscribing for the second time, we will not be able to issue them a refund. A functionality that will stop users from being able to purchase a subscription for the second time after receiving a refund for the non-trial version is in the works.

Additionally, the refunds should be done to the rider’s payment method, not Bolt Balance. 

Everything, including where and how to check the relevant information and issue the refund, has been added to the 🚗 [Information about Bolt Plus|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/7444830061330] article; see _Refunds_ section.

If you are referencing the weekly courier's report:

[^6651_report Fleet Courier Earnings Payouts And Balance (2023.49).csv]

I have checked the % difference and checked this question with the Engineers.


!image-20231214-090708.png|width=947,height=424!

 As per them, courier earnings for a single order consist of many components:

# the courier team calculates the courier earnings and sends it to us
# there are the price components that are on the eater invoice - delivery fee, small order fee, service fee. to those city VAT applies IF the courier is VAT applicable.
# then we calculate the bonus that goes on the courier aggregate invoice. bonus = courier earnings - price components on the eater invoice. invoice issuer compensation VAT is then applied to the bonus



so courier earnings with VAT really isn’t an amount that makes any sense, the differences are probably because there are different proportions between the bonus and the eater components. This report is not created by billing. it is combined by the delivery-courier team based on data that indeed billing-delivery providers, but it is hard to say how they combine it since billing does not have an entry called “courier earnings” at all. also, this table doesn’t have references to order ID-s or even order dates so it is hard to cross-reference the data.



But in general: 

The courier earnings is the sum of the delivery fee, small order fee, service fee and marketplace fee. The amount without VAT is the components without VAT and the amount with VAT is the components with VAT

But the eater invoiced components - delivery, service and small order fee - have different VAT rates than bonus aka. marketplace fee which is invoiced on the aggregate invoice. This is a combination of numbers with different VAT rates so calculating the VAT rate for this value just doesn’t make any sense.

Hey [~accountid:6126107624912a0069eedb8f] 

Went through the [ToS|https://www.apollo.io/terms] - *(i) some immediate red flags and (ii) some questions (which might or might not lead to further red flags).* 

*Let’s perhaps clear the questions bit first and only then make conclusions though I’m afraid eventually some informed risk decision needs to be taken should we wish to use their services (as we don’t seem to have the bargaining power to actually amend anything in the ToS).* Their ToS is extremely protective of their interests (see also clauses 9 and 10). However how practical the risks are largely comes down to the answers to my below questions.

Cheers!

*(i) Questions*

* What services are we actually procuring here? You mentioned _lead generation_, the order form lists (i) _Apollo Unlimited Custom,_ (ii) _Apollo: User License,_ (iii) _Job Change Alerts,_ (iv) _CRM Enrichment._ None of these indicate much what they actually stand for [other than _User License_ which I assume is just the license for using their platform as such), nor are these defined in the agreement text.
* *Clause 1.j - Submitted Data.* Related to the previous, what exact data do we feed to Apollo? Any personal data? _Need to be mindful also of c. 6.b and 6.c which provides how Apollo could use this data, incl for machine learning. Also c. 8 might need further review by Privacy etc, especially should we share any meaningful data with Apollo._
* *Clause 1.e - Output Data.* What data do we have access to on their platform? Any personal data? How do we use any data available to us via Apollo’s services? _We need to ensure ourselves that we have legal basis for processing any such data as Apollo is waiving all responsibility in this regard, see also_ *_c. 7.c_*_. Also_ *_c. 8_* _might need further review by Privacy etc depending on what exact data we receive from/via Apollo, and how we intend to use it._
* *Clause 1.k - Third-Party Products.* Do we use any such products which are not owned or operated by Apollo? _Again, Apollo waives all responsibility for these._
* What are the exact *payment terms* - what amount, when and how are we going to pay? On the order form it’s stated that the payment schedule is _semi-annual_, and the payment terms is _net 30_. Clause 3 of ToS describes the overall options, but doesn’t specify what the previous means.
* *Clause 3.c.* What exactly are “credits” and how are these used in practice? It’s like “Apollo money”?


*(ii) Identified red flags*

* *Preamble.* They keep the right to modify ToS in their sole discretion by posting updated versions on their website, and all changes shall become effective upon the posting. Effectively meaning we don’t control the content of the ToS in any given moment. Moreover, we might not even know anything has changed. _I’m not a US lawyer but I assume some sort of principal of good faith and reasonableness applies also there, meaning no such amendment can be outrageous but don’t know for sure. Also should we want to dispute any amendment we consider unjust we’d need to take it up in US._
* *Clause 2.b.* We need to insure that only Bolt group employees would have access to their platform, but e.g. not our partner market employees.
* *Clause 2.c.* Apollo waives all responsibility for the security of their service.
* *Clause 4.* Per this clause the subscription renews automatically unless cancelled 30 days prior to the end end of term - let’s acknowledge. _Also wondering how come the late subscription didn’t renew automatically?_
* *Clause 5.c.i.* Please acknowledge the listed restrictions on the use of email services (if applicable).
* *Dispute resolution (c. 11).* All disputes to be resolved in US under respective law. [~accountid:619e455ab43d5b006a05c173] *please confirm as afaik per Bolt’s contracting standard it requires AGC approval.* _I understand per_ *_c. 11.1.6_* _we have the right to opt out from the arbitration and class-action waiver clause following the formal steps provided  -_ [~accountid:6126107624912a0069eedb8f] _suggest we do that once we have decided to proceed._
* *Clause 12.* Indemnification clauses are fully one-sided. 
* *Clause 13.* Apollo has taken very wide rights as for making changes to the services.
* *Clause 16.c.* Apollo can assign the agreement as they wish, we can’t - does not comply with our standard.
* *Clause 16.f.* Apollo can send legal notices even via their services/platform which might go unnoticed compared to a dedicated email inbox.


For what it’s worth, the late added clause 1 to to the order form about Apollo using our brand for publicity, and our commitment to be participate in case studies etc - that perhaps can be adjusted more easily as it’s not part of ToS. Per your approval we can suggest to replace it with the respective clause from our [Business account contracting playbook c. 6.5|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923659743/Contracting+playbook+for+General+T+C+for+Bolt+Business.+Business+account].

Hello! 

I have reviewed the drivers that were escalated, and it appears that most of them, despite having bad orders, are also contributing positively with good orders. Our existing rules for blocking considers the ratio of a driver’s bad orders to their overall orders. These rules already are set with strict thresholds so tightening these thresholds further may potentially impact the market’s GMV.
Furthermore, it’s noteworthy that orders marked as fraud serve as a signal for driver quality and eventually impact the driver’s score. Additionally, as the orders are refunded or undergo price reviews with a 0 outcome, drivers do not receive any monetary gain and hence we do not have any monetary loss. I know that these kind of orders might be frustrating for riders so, in light of this, I recommend considering issuing warnings to these drivers to correct their behavior. In the meantime, we will add this issue to our backlog to review our thresholds again and change them if needed.

Cheers,

* _What services are we actually procuring here? None of these indicate much what they actually stand for (other than User License which I assume is just the license for using their platform as such), nor are these defined in the agreement text._

Apollo scrapes and aggregates all sort of (which seems to be exclusively) publicly available data about companies (number of employees, industry etc) from web (e.g. from LinkedIn) and also using “vetted” 3rd party providers. Such data might also include e.g. contact details of the employees of these companies (foremost emails). Data which we’d then use for lead generation to offer Business account to these companies. The _(iv) CRM Enrichment_ product we wouldn’t be using - it would enable us to feed our data to Apollo’s platform where the quality of our data could be upgraded against Apollo’s data (e.g. contacts of a company stored in our Salesforce are outdated but matching it against Apollo’s data helps us update these swiftly). *I recommend to exclude* *_CRM Enrichment_* *from the Order form.*

* _Clause 1.j - Submitted Data. Related to the previous, what exact data do we feed to Apollo? Any personal data? Need to be mindful also of c. 6.b and 6.c which provides how Apollo could use this data, incl for machine learning. * _Clause 1.e - Output Data. What data do we have access to on their platform? Any personal data? How do we use any data available to us via Apollo’s services? See the response to the first point - nothing sensitive.

Like “Apollo money”. Can be considered harmless.


*Overall* it’s obviously not a good sign that provider wants to steer clear from any liability whatsoever while we can’t have full visibility how and from there they are actually scraping all their data they are making available for us. However should any worst case scenario materialize (e.g. a 3rd party submitting a claim against us due to using their data w/o legal basis, up to Apollo altering the functionality of their product so that it would deprive us from what we contracted them for, we should acknowledge that any recourse towards Apollo can be considered highly problematic under Apollo’s ToS, and per minimum would require us to resolve that in US.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *21st of November 2023.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We share the copy of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes: 

* *Order data on 2023-10-16 requested and accepted at 09:00:46 [Exported time: UTC. Current local summer time: UTC+1]*

As it also relates to a third party subject, a passenger, with their drop off location displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty notice. 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.



Yours sincerely,

Bolt

Hey, [~accountid:5fbf9493f8b0120069af2a45]. We can download only if the above two conditions are met:

* providers confirm they own the rights to images, i.e. the provider has made photos and provided them to the competitor, and 
* the provider signs a written confirmation that includes an *indemnification* which would protect us against damages claim if the provider’s confirmation proves wrong. We have had such cases before.

However, the above is not recommended solution. Even if the two conditions are met, there is a risk that we infringe competitors' rights simply because providers quite often don’t care or know who owns rights to the photos. There have been several cases in the past where we have received take-down claims from competitors. If there will be more and more such cases, it is very likely that soon we will receive claims for monetary compensation (which will be more costly than hiring a photographer to make photos for us).  

In general, the key of the issue is that photos are protected by copyright. Copyright to images is *property* that we cannot use (scrape, download, copy, use on our platform) without the copyright owner’s consent. Very simply, it’s the same situation that we are not allowed to take an unlocked bicycle from the street and ride with it without knowing who is the bike owner and without the owner’s permission. If we want to scrape/download images from the competitor’s website to use those images on our platform, we firstly have to make sure who is the copyright owner. We cannot automatically assume that the restaurant whose products are shown in the photos owns the rights. 

Please note that this question has been raised by members of the Delivery team numerous times and Legal is working on a confluence page for data/picture scraping (ETA Q1/2024).

Dear *Sami Mirzad,* 

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *21st of November 2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We share the copy of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order data on 2023-10-16 requested and accepted at 09:00:46 [Exported time: UTC. Current local summer time: UTC+1]*

As it also relates to a third party subject, a passenger, with their drop off location displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty notice.

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *25th of November 2023.*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

Hello, 

Thank you for your ticket. 

I am aware of these issues, as they have been going on for months (if not years), and I will try to give you a quick overview of what is happening. 

----

*Explanation of why we ask a vague question*

{quote}_The instructions advise the agent to ask a vague question and to inform the user about the suspension of their account. What we have noticed is that there is no explanation for why we are not allowed to address the exact report in the first contact._{quote}

There are different reasons why we are currently not giving out details about sensitive cases, but the most important one is not to put the victim at risk. 

The issue has been raised to both Legal and Privacy. You can see the ticket [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-19775].

----

{quote}_There is also another reason which has not been specified in the instructions:_

_Within the first 24 hours of the journey, both users (rider and driver) can contact each other through the Bolt app (e.g. for lost property). When the accused party receives a message or call to elaborate on the sensitive report, then the accused party may go and confront the accusing party about the report. This is also a reason why the agent has to ask a vague question._

_Once 24 hours have passed from the journey, the rider and the driver can no longer contact each other via the Bolt app and this is when the agent could address the report with the accused party (provide the date of the report and ask why the accusing party might have made a report like this)._{quote}

This has never been an official procedure. 24h or not, the driver has still access to the address. Things might change after the “hide rider address” feature goes live, however, this has also been raised to Legal and Privacy for review, so they are aware. 

----

{quote}*Proposed solutions*

Product feature that allows the agents to disable the users to contact each other via the Bolt app when handling a sensitive safety report

Updated instructions in the Beehive Knowledge base explaining why the agents need to ask a vague question and when the agents can address the report with the accusing party{quote}

* About the first point, I agree and I raised it once already. Ideally, once we unmatch the driver and passenger, we also disable the contact feature. I will raise it again with the product team. 
* About the second point:
** We can add that we don’t want to put the reporting party in danger, but would it make a difference?
** For now I will not add the second point, as it has never been part of the official procedure. 

In short, any change has to be validated by Legal and Privacy, considering risks *and* new regulations that will come into effect (Digital Service Act). 

----

*Conflicting instructions*

{quote}_We have also noticed that there are a few event categories that have conflicting instructions when contacting the accused party._ 

_Driver Sexually Touching or Exposing Themselves_

_Driver Use Of Any Sexual Talk_

_Rider Sexually Touching or Exposing Themselves_

_Rider Use of Any Sexual Talk_

_The instructions advise the agent to do the following:_

_- Inform the reported user about the suspension of their account;_

_- Ask the user why there might have been a report like that; try engaging them in a conversation, e.g. Was there anything unusual from any of their recent journeys? Did anything out of the ordinary happen?_

_The second point is conflicting. The first part advises the agent to ask why the accusing party might have made a report like that, but the second part advises the agent to ask a vague question. This is confusing the agents._{quote}

Not sure why this is conflicting, 

* The first point says to tell the driver they’re suspended, which we do for all events. 
* The second point says to ask vague questions

Could you please explain why it’s confusing?

----

Happy to include you in any conversation with legal going further, but I think that some changes might happen not before the next quarter. 

Let me know if you have any questions and feel free to add further questions or concerns either to this ticket or [+to the one with legal+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-19775]. 

----

Cheers, 

Alessandro

Dear Sajid Hussain,



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *15th September 2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We share the copy of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order data for the whole month of July 2023 with 9th - 15th July trips also containing locations [Exported time: UTC. Current local summer time: UTC+1]*

*As it also relates to third party subjects, passengers, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of satisfying your insurer’s request in relation to an accident and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending against the claim made against you.*

*We would like to point out that the information pertaining to the location of the commencement and termination of the trips, includes third party data (passengers') and is normally excluded from the order history data we share, unless we have a compelling reason to override this, by balancing the risks in respect of your rights.  For the purposes of satisfying the insurer's request, the locations are therefore included for the order history period of 9th July to 15th July 2023 only, as per the relevant context relating to the pick up and drop off location data being of particular interest to you. We are therefore sharing the relevant data you are seeking, while adhering to the restrictions imposed by the applicable data protection rules, with the file containing the order history for month July 2023 and the location details for 9th and 15th July 2023 required for the insurance purposes.*

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link] which includes further information about:

* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

Yours sincerely,

hey [~accountid:5f718abb25fbdf00681557a5] 

Under the GDPR we have to keep user’s data (not the account) once requested and we do not need this data for other purposes (legal requirement, our legitimate purposes). In our case we can keep the account longer until the debt is paid by the user, however, we should align on the following:

# Why do we need the whole account to be remained? Can we delete the account and work on debt settling in another way: issue an invoice to the user to pay to Bolt?
## The reason I’m asking is that we can keep only certain personal data that is necessary for our purpose. In this case, we don’t need to keep the whole account and it’s better to come up with the solution where we settle the debt separately from the account
# The period of time during which we will not delete personal data or account. As I see. Epp said that we have 3 years to claim the debt, then statutory limitation expires. In our case we should delete the account max after 3 years or when the debt is paid.
## In this case we should agree with the Commerce on the scenario.
# Please note that the 1st proposal is the most suitable from the privacy side (LOW risk). However, if we cannot come up with the solution, we can rely on the 2nd proposal, but it’s risky (MEDIUM-HIGH) as we do not have a legitimate purpose to keep the whole account for debt collection.

Hi [~accountid:63abfbea7cde7bff9d78a2af] I apologise for returning to the matter only now.

Advertising/promotion of alcohol is prohibited in Poland (with some exceptions) and in any case it cannot be targeted at minors. In this case we have a non-alcoholic beverages - so formally neither sales nor promotion is restricted. However:

* there is a [clear recommendation from PAPRA|http://parpa.pl/index.php/aktualnosci/1178-stanowisko-parpa-ws-sprzedazy-piwa-bezalkoholowego ] (State Agency for Solving Alcohol Problems) that both sales and promotion should not be targeted at minors (as this shapes drinking habits);
* there are industry self-regulation with respect to non-alcohol beverages [example|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C024SRQA2G6/p1693324068748869?thread_ts=1691495023.565269&cid=C024SRQA2G6]
* the pure use of the word related to alcohol (such as ‘beer’) and in addition - linking this to an alcoholic beverages producer (e.g. Calsberg) - can be understood as an indirect form of alcoholic alcohol advertising (which cannot be targeted at minors either).

Therefore, ideally 

* (i) the advertisement/ promotion of the non-alcohol beverages should pop up in the alcohol tab in the app, 
* (i) alcohol tab should be accessible only to adult users (age verification), 
* (iii) there are age / health disclaimers on the banner, and 
* (iii) the non-alcohol beverages should only be distributed/sold to adult users (age verification).

We can revisit this advice if there are any business reasons on the case-by-case basis (as we did in case of [the Garage Energy banner / sampling campaign|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C024SRQA2G6/p1693300706375399?thread_ts=1691495023.565269&cid=C024SRQA2G6]).

Please let me know if you have any further questions.

Magda

One of the DAG runs went into a defunct state and the next one was stuck due to the depend_on_past being enabled (by default). It was in this blocked state for 130 days. The subsequent runs were blocked and started to timeout after we recently introduced a default timeout of 1 day.

So now they’re blocked for a day because of depends_on_past and then time out. So nothing broke recently, it’s an old problem that surfaced after introducing timeouts.

To solve it, you can clear the failed runs so it catches up. Alternatively, you can disable depends_on_past [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/4384229170/Scheduling#Blocking-failed-runs|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DATA/pages/4384229170/Scheduling#Blocking-failed-runs|smart-link]

*SUMMARY of Risks connected with giving benefits to drivers (minimum wage, holiday pay, and pensions)*

Bolt’s ability to defend against reclassification proceedings depends on its ability, mainly, to demonstrate the absence of a requirement for personal service. 

The provision of minimum wage, holiday pay, and pension arrangements could be a factor supporting an employee or worker relationship.

In determining the case, the courts will assess the overall relationship between the client and the contractor. 
The UK case law suggests that these benefits are customary in worker or employee relationships and atypical arrangements between a client and a professional business this could suggest that there is a worker or employee-like arrangement.
Therefore, what it suggests is that there is a risk of increasing reclassification risks by introducing these “employment benefits”. 

*Minimum wage and holiday pay -* This risk is higher, especially in the case of offering minimum wage, and holiday pay benefits. 

Furthermore, the standard regulation stipulates that employees should have the opportunity to use their holidays, and only if they are unable to do so, the employer must compensate them for the unused holidays. If Bolt diverges from this standard rule, it diminishes the risk of the benefit being labeled as employment benefits, however, the question is whether such payment would be considered as holiday pay at all and whether would Bolt be able to offset those payments in case of reclassification. 

*Pensions* - In terms of pensions, the risk is somewhat reduced due to Bolt's planned model for pension benefits. Bolt intends to provide these benefits on an opt-in basis, differing from the legally mandated approach where employees are automatically enrolled and can opt-out.

I would like to inform you that obtaining *written* consent to share a phone number is a Privacy requirement. Bolt has a responsibility to prove that the driver gave consent, and having it in a written form is needed due to our *data storage procedures*. Currently, we're unable to retain the portion of the phone call recording in which the driver agrees to share their phone number. Hence, it is necessary to request additional written consent to fulfill this requirement. This was confirmed with the Privacy team.

We are fully aware that this process can cause issues. Nevertheless, please be assured that we're actively addressing this matter and currently the Supportability team is exploring one of the possible solutions. While there is no specific timeframe for this just yet, rest assured that we're committed to enhancing this aspect.

If you have any further questions, feel free to reach out again.

with match_faces as (

    , null as val

    , id as task_id
    , 'liveness_probability' as field
    , get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.liveness_probability') as confidence
    , null as val
  from ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t
  where created >= date_add(DAY, -30, current_date) and action = 'predict_selfie_liveness'
)
, front_document_liveness as (
  select action
    , flow_run_id
    , id as task_id
    , 'front_document_liveness' as field
    , get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.front_prediction.document_liveness_response.confidence') as confidence
    , get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.front_prediction.document_liveness_response.is_live') as val
  from ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t
  where created >= date_add(DAY, -30, current_date) and action = 'predict_document_liveness'
)
, back_document_liveness as (
  select action
    , flow_run_id
    , id as task_id
    , 'back_document_liveness' as field
    , get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.back_prediction.document_liveness_response.confidence') as confidence
    , get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.back_prediction.document_liveness_response.is_live') as val
  from ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t
  where created >= date_add(DAY, -30, current_date) and action = 'predict_document_liveness'
)
, front_extract_document_fields as (
select action
	, flow_run_id
	, id as task_id
	, explode(json_object_keys(get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.front_prediction.ocr_response.predictions'))) as field
from ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t
where created >= date_add(DAY, -30, current_date) and action = 'extract_document_fields'
)
, back_extract_document_fields as (
  select action
	, flow_run_id
	, id as task_id
	, explode(json_object_keys(get_json_object(result, '$.task_data.back_prediction.ocr_response.predictions'))) as field
from ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t
where created >= date_add(DAY, -30, current_date) and action = 'extract_document_fields'
)
, front_fields_with_values as (
select de.action
  , de.flow_run_id
  , task_id
  , field
  , get_json_object(t.result, concat('$.task_data.front_prediction.ocr_response.predictions.', field, '.confidence')) as confidence
  , get_json_object(t.result, concat('$.task_data.front_prediction.ocr_response.predictions.', field, '.value')) as val
from front_extract_document_fields de
  inner join ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t on de.task_id = t.id and de.flow_run_id= t.flow_run_id and t.action = de.action)
, back_fields_with_values as (
select de.action
  , de.flow_run_id
  , task_id
  , field
  , get_json_object(t.result, concat('$.task_data.back_prediction.ocr_response.predictions.', field, '.confidence')) as confidence
  , get_json_object(t.result, concat('$.task_data.back_prediction.ocr_response.predictions.', field, '.value')) as val
from back_extract_document_fields de
  inner join ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t on de.task_id = t.id and de.flow_run_id= t.flow_run_id and t.action = de.action)
, detect_face as (
select action
    , flow_run_id
    , id as task_id
    , explode(json_object_keys(get_json_object(result, '$.task_data'))) as field
  from ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t
  where created >= date_add(DAY, -30, current_date) and action = 'detect_face')
, detect_face_vals as (
select de.action
  , de.flow_run_id
  , task_id
  , field
  , null as confidence
  , get_json_object(t.result, concat('$.task_data.', field)) as val
from detect_face de
  inner join ng_pii_spark.identity_verification_task t on de.task_id = t.id and de.flow_run_id= t.flow_run_id and t.action = de.action)
select *

Hi! I’ll try to clarify how the insurance works. We’re currently speaking about two different insurance policies (one was active when you were submitting your choices for onboarding and the other is active now). Each insurance period is a year long, this is just how health insurance works and we renew it for a new insurance policy every year. However, every time it renews we need to ask employees to let us know if they want to continue with the health insurance or switch to stebby sports compensation (and vice versa). 
Before you joined you filled out the form that asked for your preference for the insurance period that was ongoing then. You were added to the insurance as you requested. But, it just so happened that the insurance period was expiring that month, because for the health insurance it runs every year from June to end of May. So in May there was another form to confirm your wishes for the new insurance period. We cannot add you to the new health insurance without your formal request (in this case the additional form that was sent out. I’ll add a link to one of the Slack messages that went out just so you get a better understanding of what I mean: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CS4J6QPEW/p1684745267012479|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CS4J6QPEW/p1684745267012479|smart-link]). The policy changes every year and the conditions differ between policies so we can’t add a person without their consent. Especially since once you’re added to the insurance package you can’t switch until it ends in the end of May. 
So basically it was just bad timing and the communication could have been more clear for new joiners that they will soon need to pick the benefit for the new year. I have already shared this feedback with the people who will be planning the next insurance period. 

So, I will add you to the current Confido policy. Your insurance will be active from 01.01.2024 and this current policy will end on 30.05.2024. Before that, sometime in May, you’ll get to choose your benefit for the next year (June 2024-May 2025). So you’ll just have to renew your choice every year. 

I’m really sorry that this happened and I truly hope that these things will be communicated more clearly in the future. But, I hope I could help out at least now and if you have any other questions or problems with logging into Confido in January, let me know in Slack or just open a new ticket. 🙂 

Happy upcoming holidays 🎄 
Alice, People Ops

Regarding the deposits, every retailer who sells goods in returnable packaging is obliged, under the Act 477/2001 Coll. on Packaging, to buy back the packaging. However, the regulation does not take into consideration online deliveries. At the moment, there are only deposits on certain glass bottles in place. According to Consumer protection Act 643/1992 Coll, retailer is obliged to inform customer about the amount of deposit and make this information prominently visible. The deposit for the bottle is shown as a separate item on the bill. Deposit bottles are subject to the special regime for returnable packaging under the Act on VAT, 235/2004 Coll. Retailer does not apply VAT on returnable packaging, in this special VAT regime it tracks the number of packaging sold and returned during the year and at the end of the year pays VAT only on packaging that has not been returned.

We will skip showing any discounts, and at the checkout, we will reserve the total cost without loyalty discounts applied even if the user has a valid loyalty card ID entered. If, after processing the order by 3P POS system, the total basket value is less than what we reserved, we will charge the correct amount by creating a [+price basket adjustment+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hiHWBI7JsdR9RHCKiZMuItAEQ_jNHBUa94LNylFZPZg/edit#heading=h.rwcr4vw81p8z].

The process would look the following:

# We accept a Loyalty card ID in the app.
# We accept this card only for specific 3P providers (that have this feature enabled).
# We *don't* validate this card ID.
# We send it with each new order to the partner via the API.
# We book the full price of all loyalty products from the customer. 
# We send *original* prices to the partner so they can apply a discount to the loyal products at their POS.
# We don't show or apply any loyalty discounts at checkout in the Bolt Food app. => {color:#ff5630}what are the risks with this? should we add some disclaimer in the app when user is making a checkout and/or under the informal receipt we are sending to user´s email?{color}
# Partner validates the correct prices in their POS. 
# Partner sends us the final prices with loyalty discounts, and we charge the user the correct amount: We BOOK the amount from the customer without the discount, but we only CHARGE the customer once we have had the final confirmation from the partner as to the amount of the basket.
# We don't accept / require loyalty products' prices from the partner and don’t keep them in the WMS.
# *The user should be charged exactly as in the partner's final fiscal receipt issues by their POS.*
# We don’t save a loyalty card for each order in the DB.

||Policy||Description||
|*noeviction*|Redis will reject any new commands that would cause the memory usage to exceed the limit. This will cause the client to receive an error.|
|*allkeys-lru*|Redis will remove the least recently used (LRU) keys from the database until there is enough memory available. This policy is generally safe for read-heavy workloads, but it can cause performance problems for write-heavy workloads.|
|*allkeys-random*|Redis will remove random keys from the database until there is enough memory available. This policy is not as predictable as {{allkeys-lru}}, but it is still safe for read-heavy workloads.|
|*volatile-lru*|Redis will remove the LRU keys that have an expiration time set. This policy is useful for cache workloads, as it will ensure that the most recently accessed keys are not evicted.|
|*volatile-random*|Redis will remove random keys that have an expiration time set. This policy is similar to {{volatile-lru}}, but it is not as predictable.|

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance, a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

Answers from Ravio:
*- Which data gets anonymised, in which cases and how? What anonymisation techniques are they implementing?*

Please refer to the attached Data Flow Diagram which outlines the data anonymization process at a high-level. Data within the 'Explore the Market' section of the platform (the benchmarking data) is aggregated and anonymised. We remove any potential identifiers from that data including name, company name, and only include job titles from our 'standardised' Ravio job title library to further eliminate any risk of identification. We also only display benchmarks for roles which have a minimum number of underlying data points.

*- What’s the retention period for the data they access from us?*

As Ravio is the data processor, we retain the data provided until such a point that the Customer (you) request that it is deleted *or* you stop using the Ravio platform, at which point the data is removed within 30 days of this request. Please refer to clauses 7.2 and 9.1(b) of the DPA within the Service Agreement, linked [here|https://d30-xf04.eu1.hs-sales-engage.com/Ctc/GG+23284/d30-xf04/JkM2-6qcW6N1vHY6lZ3pfW1N65ZT90wcnpW9k6BlR5lZ5kMW6HfLmn1TB328W6bMgQ48Fj89hW49z3sQ1SPrQwW4NsDVK2jM4Q5VYf9c13dWPrrW3JqZPK7Vt4H7W8V11kQ3bsBsjW19v3MW6PQqrlW377QKf7vFZXpW6B9R8n2hsMGbW92r33s17j_QmW3-9x1M2GkJkyW5NDDGg66cZbXW7VwR186K0wdgW9dXrlW4xbHkJW72xC2r1GmQcjW2jqJ7r4bXFFQVKSg9s6Ksg_cW5wp9z97wgHhgW4WnpXn1RLwXBd__GDq04].

*- Is there a chance that an employee gets identified? This is not clear to me.*

Please refer to that attached data flow diagram. Once the data has been anonymised and aggregated within the Explore the Market section, there is no way to re-identify the data subject, and therefore there is no proposed identification of your employees by other customers. Your own users will be able to see your employees within the 'Analyse my Company' section of the platform, identified either by name or by employee ID (if you choose not to provide name), this enables them to compare the individual to the benchmark. Internally we use role-based access control restricted based on the principle of least privilege and we conduct quarterly access control reviews and take data and security extremely seriously.

*- If RavioIQ is not based on employee data, why do they need the employee data or how do they do the calculations? or do you mean they don't need the data of employees when the sample is very low and there is the risk of identifying them?*

Yes, RavioIQ is used in situations where there is not enough underlying data to provide a benchmark, and is replaced by the data in those areas as we grow and get more data in those areas. It is ordinarily used in niche roles or emerging markets where we don't yet have full coverage.



*- I would also like to draw to your attention the provision in the Agreement that we agree that Ravio will use anonymised Customer Personal Data for the purposes of enhancing its database(s) of anonymised employee compensation data. Given that the data used for these purposes is anonymised, it does not meet the definition of ‘personal data’ as defined in the Data Protection Laws (as defined in the DPA), and so the Data Protection Laws do not apply in respect of this anonymised data.*

Agreed - it is only considered anonymous once we have removed the identifiable data however, please refer to the response above.

Dear *Eniola Aderolu Adesina,*



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *19/09/2023.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order history data from April 15th to 19th, 2023 [Exported time: UTC. Current local summer time: UTC+1]*

*As it also relates to third party subjects, passengers, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice (ticket) received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty notice.*

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link]  , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.



Yours sincerely,

Bolt
