Dear *Peter Bbaale Kakeeto,* 



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *20th September 2023.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order data in June 2023, with 5th June 2023 data also containing the locations [Exported time: UTC. Current local summer time: UTC+1]*

*As it also relates to third party subjects, passengers, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice (parking ticket) received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty notice.*

*We would like to point out that the information pertaining to the location of the commencement and termination of the trips, includes third party data (passengers') and is normally excluded from the order history data we share, unless we have a compelling reason to override this, by balancing the risks in respect of your rights.  For the purposes of defending against a parking ticket, the locations are therefore included for the order history on 5th June 2023 only, as per the relevant context relating to the pick up and drop off location data being of particular interest to you.* 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.



Yours sincerely,

Bolt

* *full documentation package for all drivers (there are many stories in Portugal of drivers driving without being registered in the system)*

All TVDE drivers in Portugal need to fulfil the requirements established by Law n.o 45/2018 de 10 de agosto. In particular, every driver needs to hold a driving license for at least 3 years, a certificate of TVDE driver issued by the national authority, a course certificate to become a TVDE driver issued by a third party and no criminal record. 

In compliance with the current legislation, Bolt requires these documents for all drivers in the platform, which are verified at the moment a driver account is activated and later on at the time of expiry of such documents. 

Due to privacy related principles, we are unfortunately not able to share this personal data with passengers and make available the documentation for each driver.

* *Control of cars so that there is no extra hours (there are stories of two or three drivers driving one car so that the car is not idle, but only one driver is registered in the system)*

The profession of TVDE drivers is regulated in Portugal. Consequently, only drivers with an account in the platform and fulfilling the legal requirements are able to legally provide transportation services. 

In addition to the documentation compliance in place, we have recently introduced identity verification for drivers. This means that drivers in the platform submit a real-time selfie as part of our identity verification process during registration, as well as later on and on a regular basis. 

Passengers are also important partners in maintaining the safety of the platform. We recommend each passenger to check that the driver’s face, car make and registration plate match those shown in the app. When in doubt passengers send us reports that prompt us to to double check the concerns raised.

* *Audio or video monitoring in the car during trips, for the safety of both passenger and driver*

Even though we are committed with the highest safety standard, we must ensure any such measures are implemented in accordance with local regulations. Even though many markets may not enable electronic platforms to implement such type of features, we have recently introduced a safety feature that allow passengers to share trip details. This allows passengers to send the car's make, model, registration number, and live location to friends or family via a shareable link.

* *Instruction to drivers on what they can and cannot do*

Following local regulations, TVDE drivers in electronic platforms work at the service of certified TVDE operators in Portugal. These TVDE operators are independent companies from Bolt and the drivers at their service therefore autonomous from Bolt. 

Nevertheless, the profession of TVDE driver is regulated in Portugal and therefore TVDE operators and their drivers compelled to provide their services in compliance with legislation in place.

select 
	rc.compensation_date_date,
	rc.to_agent_id, 
	rc.to_agent_type, 
	cit.title,
	i.vat_pct as VAT_percent,
	i.sum as sum_lcc, 
	i.vat_sum as vat_sum_lcc, 
	i.sum_with_vat as sum_with_vat_lcc,
	i.sum_eur as sum_eur, 
	i.vat_sum_eur as vat_sum_eur, 
	i.sum_with_vat_eur as sum_with_vat_eur,
	i.city_name as city
from glue.commerce_finance.finance_model_pl_rides_interm_invoicing_record i
left join glue.ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_record_compensation rc on i.tran_row_id=rc.record_id 
left join (select uid, uid_type, client_id, date, group_id, fee_type, fee_subtype, created_date, title, sum  from glue.ng_public.invoicing_compensation_import_item 
			where created_date >= date '2022-12-30') cit on cit.uid=rc.compensation_uid and cit.group_id=rc.group_id and rc.compensation_date_date=cit.date

	on fmap.rs_pl_type = i.tran_row_type and fmap.rs_pl_subtype = i.tran_row_subtype and fmap.rs_pl_finance_type = i.finance_type and fmap.rs_pl_source = i.tran_type 
where i.tran_local_date >= date '2023-01-01' 
	and i.tran_local_date < date '2023-12-01'
	--and co.created_date is not null
	and fmap.wd_cost_revenue_account=4140
	--and i.tran_row_type  in ('fleet_compensation','compensation') 
	and title  like '%VISA%'
	and i.country_code ='ge'{noformat}

select i.tran_local_date, i.city_name, tc.name, 
round(sum( case when i.vat_pct=0 then  i.sum/1.18 else i.sum end),2) as sum_gel, 
round(sum( case when i.vat_pct=0 then  i.sum_eur/1.18 else i.sum_eur end),2) as sum_eur, 
round(sum( case when i.vat_pct=0 then  i.sum-i.sum/1.18 else i.vat_sum end),2) as vat_sum_gel, 
round(sum( case when i.vat_pct=0 then  i.sum_eur-i.sum_eur/1.18 else i.vat_sum_eur end),2) as vat_sum_eur, 
round(sum( case when i.vat_pct=0 then  i.sum_with_vat else i.sum_with_vat end),2) as sum_with_vat_gel, 
round(sum( case when i.vat_pct=0 then  i.sum_with_vat_eur else i.sum_with_vat_eur end),2) as sum_with_vat_eur  
from glue.commerce_finance.finance_model_pl_rides_interm_invoicing_record i
left join (select invoice_external_id, id, city_id, vat_percentage, from_agent_type, to_agent_type, from_agent_id, to_agent_id, type, order_id

left join (select * from glue.ng_public.company_order where created_date >= date '2023-08-30' and created_date < date '2023-11-02') oo on oo.id=r.order_id and oo.city_id=r.city_id
left join glue.ng_public.campaign_targeted_campaign tc on tc.code=split(oo.campaign_code,'-')[1]
where i.country_code ='ge' and i.tran_local_date  >= date '2023-01-01' and i.tran_local_date < date '2023-12-01' and r.type in ('rider_campaign_compensation','fleet_rider_campaign_compensation','rider_campaign')
and tc.name like '%VISA%'

For background, drivers are generally prohibited by Bolt from doing anything which is ‘unlawful' when providing services via our platform. However, as our drivers are not employees and (in most markets) do not work *_for_* Bolt, we do not typically provide overly strict rules on how drivers interact with passengers. We should also be mindful that some interactions may be consented to a passengers at the time. On the data-specific side, there are typically provisions our terms to ensure that drivers must not use personal data of passengers in any way other than the provision of services.

Regardless, we can potentially treat such occurrences as a safety incident, if that seems like a reasonable thing to do in the given circumstances. Where this makes sense, it can be shared with our safety team as an incident so they can decide on the best course of action.

My understanding is that the matter comes down to product safety legislation and our obligations as a service operator / provider of rental services to inform about possible hazards using our scooters. Under Swedish law we must inform consumers about important safety aspects/hazards of a product or service we are providing - unless the risk is obvious. For example, if the breaks are not safe or can easily break down, this is not an obvious hazard, and we must warn users about the safety hazards related to using our scooters e.g. with signs or stickers, messages/information in the app, in the media, through comms, or otherwise. On the contrary, we don't need a sign on the scooters telling users that they need to wear a helmet because it's obviously risky to ride without a helmet.I don't see anything in the relevant legislation obligating us to leave out technical data specifically, but rather that we are obliged to inform the user about the nature of the safety hazard they suffered from and what we are doing to prevent that it happens again.You can read some further guidance on the above topic (in English) at the Swedish consumer agency's webpage, here: [https://www.hallakonsument.se/en/articles/product-safety-act/|https://www.hallakonsument.se/en/articles/product-safety-act/|smart-link]

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *21/11/2023.*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Yours sincerely,

{noformat}select city_name, date_trunc('month',created),
sum(case when to_state in ('paused') then time_till_next_state else null end) 
from (
select *, 
lead(to_state) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) next_state,
lead(created) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) next_created,
date_diff('second',created,lead(created) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc)) time_till_next_state
from (
--select c.name,e.created ,e.vehicle_id ,e.value_new as to_state
--from ng_carsharing.rental_car_vehicle_vehicle_state_event e
--join ng_carsharing.rental_fleet_car_search_category sc on e.search_category_id =sc.id
--join ng_public.admin_system_city c on sc.city_id =c.id
--where e.created_date >date'2023-01-01' and e.created_date <date'2023-12-01'
--and type='state'
--union all 
select c.name as city_name, e.created, o.vehicle_id, e.event as to_state
from ng_carsharing.rental_car_order_order_event e
join  ng_public.admin_system_city c on e.city_id =c.id
join  ng_carsharing.rental_car_order_order o on e.order_id =o.id and e.city_id =o.city_id 
where  e.created_date >date'2023-01-01' and e.created_date <date'2023-12-01'

* *Background*: This Red Flag Review was conducted at the last-minute due to insufficient time to markup and negotiate AuditBoard’s DPA. The purpose is to draw the Business' attention to key risks involved in AuditBoard’s processing activities.
* *Overview*: In summary, the DPA is largely okay, however, there are a few key risks highlighted below for the Business' attention and approval. Where possible, we have indication remediations to be made by AuditBoard. 
* *Current Risk Level*: Considering the limited personal data being shared (employee names and contact details/work email addresses), the risk of the processing is *generally low*. However, if Bolt were to share any documentation/files or other data containing personal data of Bolt employees or any third parties, the risk of this processing activity would be considered higher and we would highly recommend that at a minimum, the below risks are dealt with before any other data is shared with AuditBoard. 

||*Clause*||*Risk*||*Commentary*||
|*1.* "Security Policy" means AuditBoard's Security Policy currently located at: [https://auditboard.com/enterprise-agreements/ |https://auditboard.com/enterprise-agreements]. AuditBoard may update the Security Policy from time to time provided that such updates do not result in a material reduction of the security of the Services.|This Security Policy is not aligned to Bolt’s Information Security Code of Practice and has not been reviewed by Privacy. Accordingly, without InfoSec approval, there is a risk that the security obligations set out in AuditBoard’s policy may not meet Bolt’s security standards.
Because the Policy may be unilaterally updated by AuditBoard from time to time (as it is incorporated by way of a hyperlink) there is also a risk that AuditBoard’s security obligations may change over time.|{color:#ff5630}*Please ensure that InfoSec has approved the Policy.*{color}|
|*6.1* Customer hereby agrees and provides a general authorization that AuditBoard and Audit Board’s Affiliates may engage Subprocessors. 
AuditBoard will provide notice to Customer at least 30 days prior to authorizing any new Subprocessor to process Personal Data by updating the Subprocessor List.|Bolt faces risks stemming from the broad authorization it gives, allowing AuditBoard and its Affiliates to engage Subprocessors without notifying Bolt (in writing). 
Bolt is expected to monitor an webpage containing AuditBoard’s subprocessor list, which is impractical.
This may lead to limited control over Subprocessors, lack of transparency regarding their identity and location, potential exposure to inadequate data protection standards in various jurisdictions, and challenges in ensuring uniform compliance and security practices among Subprocessors.|Notwithstanding the risk identified, due to the limited nature of personal data being shared with AuditBoard (employee names/work email addresses), and the fact that “AuditBoard will enter into a written contract with each Subprocessor which imposes on such Subprocessor terms no less protective of Personal Data than those imposed on AuditBoard in this DPA”, {color:#4c9aff}*the risk is low*{color}.|
|*7.4 EU Personal Data.* In relation to Personal Data that is protected by the EU GDPR, the EU SCCs will apply completed as follows:
(i) Module 2 applies unless the Customer is a Processor in which case Module 3 applies; (ii) in Clause 7, the optional docking clause will apply; (iii) in Clause 9, Option 2 will apply, and the time period for prior notice of subprocessor changes will be in accordance with the notification process set out in Section 6.1 of this DPA; (iv) in Clause 11, the optional redress language will not apply; (vi) in Clause 17, Option 1 will apply, and the Standard Contractual Clauses will be governed by the law specified in the MSA, provided that law is an EEA Member State law recognizing third party beneficiary rights, otherwise, the laws of Ireland apply; (vi) in Clause 18(b), disputes shall be resolved before the courts specified in the MSA, provided these courts are located in an EU Member State, otherwise those courts shall be the courts of Ireland; (vii) Annex I of the Standard Contractual Clauses shall be deemed completed with the information set out in Annex I to this DPA; and (viii) Annex II of the Standard Contractual Clauses shall be deemed completed with the information set out in the Security Policy.|The application of the EU SCCs is normal practice, however, the jursidiction for any disputes arising out of the SCCs is unclear and ambigous. This is because the clause makes reference to the “MSA”, which is not a defined term in the DPA. 
The DPA only refers to the “Agreement” - the Subscription Agreement. 
If this point is not clarified, it would be quite contentious to bring a claim against AuditBoard as they would be able to argue that the Court selected by Bolt does not have jurisdiction to hear the matter.|We would recommend amending 7.4 to refer to the “Agreement” and not the “MSA” to resolve this issue. {color:#ff991f}*The risk if not amended is medium*{color}.|
|*8. AUDIT AND RECORDS*|The audit rules in the DPA create challenges for Bolt. Only one audit is allowed per year without extra charges, which could make it hard for Bolt to assess things more often, reducing how well it can oversee things. Any extra audits would cost Bolt money. 
Bolt is not allowed to conduct an emergency audit, which is problematic in the event a Regulator requires such an audit. Bolt is required to enter into a confidentiality agreement with a Regulator who wants to audit Bolt and AuditBoard as Bolt’s supplier — this is very difficult to guarantee and could land Bolt in breach of this clause.

Bolt is also limited to relying on AuditBoard's then-current Audit Reports. If the reports are considered insufficient by Bolt, the process for conducting an independent audit is outlined, but it involves negotiation, potential costs, and dependency on AuditBoard's agreement.|It is unlikely that AuditBoard would accept any changes to this clause, but {color:#ff991f}*the risks should be noted and can be categorized as medium*{color} (considering the likelihood of them occuring).|
|*Annex 1 - Description of Processing*|According to feedback from [~accountid:712020:46ca1bd4-650e-4217-b42f-78a9deb502a3] , “_Data will be hosted in Dublin. Only possibility to move the data outside of EEA would be if the request is coming from Bolt_”. However, Annex 1 does not mention the storage location of Bolt’s data and only speaks to AuditBoard’s US entity in CA importing Bolt’s data. 
There is also no obligation or warranty (promise) from AuditBoard indicating that they have, or will, conduct a Transfer Impact Assessment before exporting data out of the EEA/UK, to the USA. [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] I think that original basis was the [EU DIRECTIVE 93/13/EEC on unfair terms in consumer contracts|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A01993L0013-20220528] - see Annex:
- section 1 (j): clauses “_enabling the seller or supplier to alter the terms of the contract unilaterally without a valid reason which is specified in the contract_” are deemed unfair;
- section 2(b) - “_Subparagraph (j) is also without hindrance to terms under which a seller or supplier reserves the right to alter unilaterally the conditions of a contract of indeterminate duration,_ *_provided that he is required to inform the consumer with reasonable notice and that the consumer is free to dissolve the contract_**.*”

What is the reasonable notice is more up to the local legislation or local legal practise. +/- 14 days notice is for CEE.

Hello Kornelia Chrustowska 

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

Regrettably, Bolt cannot agree to the technical requirement stipulating the exclusion of contractors and Bolt employees holding citizenship of Russia and Belarus from the provision of services. Such a requirement is inherently discriminatory and conflicts with both applicable laws and Bolt's core principles. Potential consequences include scrutiny by authorities such as the Equal Opportunity Ombudsman, who may investigate the legality and justification of such discriminatory clauses.

The proposed requirement contradicts EU law, particularly the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, which expressly prohibits discrimination based on nationality. Additionally, the EU Single Market and Services Directive, designed to eliminate barriers to service provision across member states, is conflicted by any requirement restricting service providers based on nationality.

Moreover, the Constitution of the Republic of Lithuania guarantees fundamental rights and freedoms to all individuals within its jurisdiction. A technical requirement discriminating against Russian or Belarusian service providers may contravene these constitutional protections, specifically those related to equality and non-discrimination.

Furthermore, adopting such a standard contradicts Bolt's core principles of equal treatment and nondiscrimination. Bolt is committed to hiring and treating employees on equal terms, prohibiting any form of discrimination, including based on nationality, social status, or ethnic origin. Our corporate culture promotes equal opportunities, diversity, and an inclusive workplace where differences are embraced and respected.

Considering the aforementioned and the lack of any objective justification for the inclusion of such a discriminatory clause, Bolt cannot accept the requirement embedded in the 1.2.6 clause of the technical investigation. We kindly urge you to reconsider and exclude the 1.2.6 clause from the technical specification since it is discriminatory.

Please note that in practical terms, the imposition of EU entry obstacles and visa challenges on citizens of Russia and Belarus already significantly limits the engagement of individuals holding citizenship of Russia and Belarus in providing services and/or being employed in Lithuania.

NO from security SD: 

While this might make the process smoother for Ops, this presents a serious security risk to the banking information and other sensitive and private data collected by such third-party tools/forms used.

These forms might not offer the same level of security as Beehive, especially when they are not designed specifically to collect and handle sensitive financial data. Although I have seen that for example, typeform has met some compliance requirements, going this route simply adds to the high-impact risks that could occur when these tools are exposed to security breaches. The risks far outweigh the business benefits outlined.

Additionally, by collecting bank details through an online form, there is an increased risk of phishing attacks. Fraudsters could create fake forms to mimic the legitimate process, tricking customers into submitting their financial details.

I suggest looking into ways to enhance the existing process while maintaining all interactions and data exchanges within Beehive or Bolt’s internal tools, under our control, and where the security team can also monitor and support security-related concerns.
